## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
This maintenance visit recorded a critical deficiency in pump operation. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This is a confirmed equipment failure requiring immediate professional attention. All other system components measured within normal parameters.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet, which is normal for a system at rest between pump cycles.

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENT

| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank (concrete, 1250 gal) | Good | No structural defects observed |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Light soiling; cleaned and reseated during this visit |
| Effluent Pump (0.5 HP, 115V) | **CRITICAL** | Running but no load detected |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and confirmed operational |
| Pump Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry; no ponding or breakout observed |

## PUMP OPERATION -- CRITICAL FINDING
The effluent pump measured 1.6 amps during operation against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This 22.2% load indicates the pump is running without hydraulic resistance. The motor is spinning but no fluid is being moved.

**Probable causes:**
- Broken or missing impeller
- Severed or disconnected discharge line
- Dry-running condition (no fluid reaching the pump intake)

**Risk:** Continued operation without load will overheat the motor and cause winding failure. The pump must not be run until the cause is identified and corrected.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (Critical Priority):**
- **Stop operating the pump immediately.** Do not run additional cycles until the no-load condition is resolved.
- A qualified technician must examine the pump discharge line for disconnection, blockage or damage.
- A qualified technician must examine the pump impeller for breakage or missing components.
- If the discharge line is intact and the impeller is present, the pump must be removed and professionally serviced or replaced.

**Routine (Next Maintenance Visit):**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once pump operation is restored and verified.
- The effluent filter performed well during this visit. Continue cleaning at each maintenance visit.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Failure
Your pump is not moving water, even though the motor is running. This is a mechanical failure that will damage the motor if it continues. Do not use the system until a technician has found and fixed the problem. This is not a maintenance issue you can defer -- it requires immediate professional repair.

### Solids Management
This maintenance visit recorded solids at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Solids accumulate naturally over time. Keeping non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease -- keeps that accumulation slow and predictable.
